scope.flow: Full withdrawal of a user's deposited assets from OffsetProgressiveCurve
scope.environment: EVM/Solidity smart contract (arithmetic on blockchain state)

statements.text: OffsetProgressiveCurve was initialized with an offset18 parameter smaller than 1e9.
During initialize, OFFSET = PCMath.divDown(OFFSET18, 1e18) truncates to 0 because OFFSET18 < 1e18, so the stored OFFSET is 0 before the withdrawal.
The user has a deposit (open position) in the curve whose full withdrawal is attempted.
A user attempts a full withdrawal of their deposit.

With OFFSET squaring to 0, the withdrawal math yields squaredShares = square(totalShares + OFFSET) strictly less than inner = mulDivUp(assets, SLOPE, 1e18) + square(OFFSET), so subtracting shares = squaredShares - inner underflows.
The full withdrawal deterministically reverts with PANIC(0x11) arithmetic underflow.
The user is permanently blocked from fully closing their position, trapping their funds when liquidating assets.
Users should be able to fully withdraw their deposited assets from OffsetProgressiveCurve without the withdrawal reverting and trapping funds (inferred from the claimed trapped-funds failure).

ambiguities: Reported bound is inconsistent: title/impact say offset18 < 1e9, but the truncation mechanism requires OFFSET18 < 1e18.
The user's exact deposited balance/share quantity is not specified; only that a full withdrawal of the deposit is attempted.
No attacker or authorization claim is made; the affected caller is merely a user with a deposit, and the impact is trapped funds rather than theft.
'Permanently blocked' is asserted; alternative exits (e.g., partial withdrawals or admin recovery) are not addressed.
Whether any full-withdrawal amount triggers the underflow, or only specific amounts, is not fully specified; the description suggests it applies generally.
